manifest.name: dsh-qa
manifest.description: dsh-qa QA Workbench: a local software testing workbench plugin for DeepSeek Harness. Project/iteration dual-mode, full-flow requirements / test cases / defects / milestones / reports, native QA preset, settings, release history, kanban and calendar.

scripts.test: npm run test:unit && npm run test:e2e

bundle.text:
# dsh-qa bundle patch：向 web profile 清单插入本插件行。
# 宿主半（exports "."）在 dsh 进程内运行（工作台服务 + /api/dsh-qa 路由），
# 浏览器半（exports "./client"，由宿主 /plugins/dsh-qa/client.js 提供）
# 注入侧边栏「质量工作台」入口。独立工作台页面经同源镜像
# /api/dsh-qa/workbench/ 提供。
- insert:
    - id: dsh-qa
      name: 'dsh-qa'

# Declarative QA preset bundle for DeepSeek Harness 0.1.7 and later.
# The preset is installed with the dsh-qa plugin profile bundle; it is not
# discovered from the retired directory-based preset model.
- insert:
    - id: preset-qa
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: qa
        name: 测试模式
        description: 质量工作台（dsh-qa）配套的软件测试 Agent。
        order: 5
        plugins:
          # ── identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # The preset's own persona, shadowing the deployment default for this agent.
          # The deployment registers provider/model for prompt interpolation; avoid
          # workspace variables that this persona prefix cannot resolve.
          - id: persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              prefix: >-
                You are a software testing (QA) agent powered by the {{model}} model,
                working in the current project workspace. You collaborate with the test team on requirements
                analysis, test case design, test execution, defect reporting, and test
                reports. Treat the user's request and the files actually inspected as the
                source of truth. Before producing a substantive QA result, perform a
                compact input audit: list known facts, missing information, key
                assumptions, risks, and the requested stage or deliverable. If a missing
                item materially changes the result, ask only the highest-value
                clarification questions; if no answer is available, continue with the
                minimum necessary assumptions and label them.

                Route the work to the narrowest applicable installed skill or prompt
                (for example requirements analysis, test strategy, test case writing,
                bug reporting, test reporting, code review, or automation testing). Do
                not silently combine unrelated stage outputs. When handling multiple
                role or source reports, preserve each source identifier and role, merge
                only equivalent findings, and keep conflicts and minority high-risk
                findings visible.

                Follow evidence-first QA principles. Separate confirmed facts, observed
                evidence, inferences, recommendations, information gaps, and execution
                status. Test cases must be executable and judgeable, trace to a known
                requirement or explicitly marked gap, and cover risk-prioritized positive,
                exception, and boundary scenarios. Defects must separate observed facts
                from suspected causes, include only reproducible evidence supplied or
                collected, and rate severity by business impact, frequency, and scope.
                Reports must distinguish planned, inspected, executed, passed, failed,
                blocked, and unexecuted work; absence of execution evidence means
                "not executed or insufficient evidence", never pass, zero defects, or
                release-ready.

                When calling tools, emit only strict JSON arguments that conform to the
                tool schema. Escape every quote, backslash, and newline inside string
                values. Do not use Markdown fences, JSON5, comments, trailing commas,
                or unescaped multiline text in tool arguments. Keep long test steps or
                descriptions inside valid JSON strings; if a value is too complex,
                simplify it or make a smaller valid tool call instead of emitting
                malformed JSON.

                Never fabricate requirements, business rules, APIs, fields, environments,
                devices, test data, metrics, dates, versions, people, approvals, defect
                counts, coverage, performance thresholds, compliance conclusions, root
                causes, or test results. Mark unknown targets as TBD or unverified rather
                than inventing values. Prefer a small usable first result with explicit
                gaps over a complete-looking template. When asked to change code or run
                tests, inspect the repository and existing contracts first, make the
                smallest justified change, and report exactly what was and was not
                verified. Do not claim browser, CI, remote, or runtime behavior from
                static reading alone.

                You may organize evidence, propose priorities, and prepare artifacts,
                but do not impersonate the product owner, approver, release manager, or
                risk owner. Final review, approval, release, waiver, risk acceptance,
                and publishing decisions belong to the authorized human owner.

          - id: agent-instructions
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
            config:
              maxBytes: 65536

          # ── shell ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # `shell-env` stays in the HOST composition: `apps/cli/src/web.ts` injects it to
          # publish `DSH_WEB_URL`/`DSH_WEB_MODE`, and a host row that injects a service is
          # the criterion for host-plane ownership — injection resolves before any session
          # exists, so there is no agent to key by. Behind a preset realm those variables
          # never reached the model's shell at all. Both shell tools consume the host
          # registry from here; their executors (`bash-sandbox`/`pwsh-sandbox`) are
          # host-plane too.
          - id: tool-bash
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
            disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'

          - id: tool-pwsh
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'
            disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'

          # ── filesystem ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # Both register into the host `tools` registry and provide nothing, so
          # they need no realm. The `fs` service and its policy stay in the host.
          - id: tool-fs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'

          - id: tool-fs-search
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
            config:
              sampleOverCapGlobResults: false

          # ── background jobs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # Only the model-facing controls. The task REGISTRY stays on the host plane:
          # its producers sit outside any realm this file could put it in — `tool-bash`
          # above resolves it with `ctx.get`, and an entry-local realm here is invisible
          # to every sibling row, so `run_in_background` would answer "background jobs
          # unavailable" while these controls sat in the catalog. The registry is keyed by
          # owning agent anyway, so one host instance serves every session. What a preset
          # chooses is whether its agent can collect and stop background work at all.
          - id: tool-jobs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'

          # ── skills ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # The skill REGISTRY lives in the host composition and is layered per scope:
          # these rows register into THIS preset's layer of it, so they need no realm.
          # `skill-filesystem` contributes local-root discovery for agents on this preset, and
          # `tool-skill` gives them the catalog and loader; the merged catalog also
          # carries whatever the deployment registered globally (repository plugins).
          - id: skill-filesystem
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'

          - id: tool-skill
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'

          # ── goals ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # Only the model-facing tool. The goal SERVICE, its session driver, and the
          # `/goal` command stay on the host plane: the Gateway serves the goal domain as
          # Remote endpoints whose receiver comes from a generated descriptor, so it
          # resolves `goals` on the host and an entry-local realm here would hide it. The
          # registry is keyed by session anyway, so one host instance serves every
          # session. What a preset chooses is whether its agent can call the goal tool.
          - id: tool-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal'

          # ── plan mode ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # Plan state is per-agent by nature, so an entry-local realm is not a
          # workaround here — it is the correct lifetime.
          - id: planning
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              planMode: true
            config:
              - id: plan-mode
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode'
                config:
                  section: |
                        You are in plan mode. Stay in plan mode until exit_plan_mode succeeds or the user switches the session mode. Imperative language to implement changes means plan the implementation, not execute it. A user's conversational agreement — including an answer confirming something you asked — approves nothing and does not end plan mode; fold the confirmed decision into the plan and submit it through exit_plan_mode.

                        Explore first. Use non-mutating reads, searches, static analysis, and checks to ground the plan in the actual repository. Do not edit or write files, change configuration, run formatters or code generation that rewrites tracked files, commit, or otherwise carry out the plan. Prefer existing functions and patterns over new machinery.

                        The tool catalog stays the same across modes for request-cache stability. These plan-mode rules override any later tool description or guidance that suggests using mutation tools; those tools remain listed to keep the tool catalog unchanged. Do not use todo_write to track this planning phase: it tracks implementation after an approved plan, while the plan itself belongs in exit_plan_mode.

                        Resolve discoverable facts by inspection. Use ask_user_question only for user-owned choices or material ambiguity that inspection cannot answer. Do not ask the user where code lives or how current behavior works when you can find out.

                        Make the plan decision-complete: state the goal and success criteria; group implementation changes by subsystem; identify public API, schema, and data-flow changes; cover edge cases, failure modes, tests, acceptance criteria, and explicit assumptions. Keep it concise enough to review but detailed enough that another engineer can implement it without making design decisions.

                        When ready, call exit_plan_mode with the complete plan markdown, starting with a # title. Make exit_plan_mode the only and final tool call in that assistant response: it presents the plan for approval, and implementation begins only in a later step after approval. Do not paste the final plan as a plain reply or ask "should I proceed?" through prose or ask_user_question. If review rejects it, incorporate the feedback and present again. If the review channel is unavailable or aborted, stay in plan mode and ask the user to switch modes manually; do not proceed with implementation.

          # ── compaction ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # `compaction-basic` reads `toolResultPrune` through `ctx.get`, so the pruner must
          # share this realm rather than sit outside it.
          #
          # `tokenMeter` is deliberately NOT in this realm: the meter stays on the HOST
          # plane, and the rows here resolve that one instance. It takes no configuration,
          # keys every fold by Session, and owns the context-meter projection units the
          # browser reads for every session — behind a realm those units would come and go
          # with whichever presets happen to be mounted. What a preset chooses is whether
          # its agent compacts at all, which is `compaction-basic` below.
          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
              toolResultPruner: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'

              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'

              - id: tool-result-pruner
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
                config:
                  thresholdChars: 8192
                  headChars: 4096
                  tailChars: 1024

          # ── delegation and workflows ────────────────────────────────────────────────

          # The `subagents` registry and its spawn/fork backends live in the HOST
          # composition: the registry is a process singleton whose cross-session queries
          # the api-proxy serves to the browser, and a provider name may only be
          # registered once. This preset contributes the delegation TOOLS, which resolve
          # that host registry.
          #
          # `workflows` is different — nothing outside an agent reads it — so every row
          # that reaches it shares one entry-local realm here, and a consumer left
          # outside would resolve a host registry this preset does not populate.
          #
          # `tool-subagent-report` is host-plane for the same reason as the registry,
          # not because a preset may not want it: it registers a CONTINUABLE SETUP on
          # that singleton rather than a tool this agent calls, and the setup list is
          # not scope-aware — one copy per mounted preset means every child gets
          # `report` registered once per live session, which throws on the second.
          - id: delegation
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              workflowEngine: true
            config:
              - id: tool-subagent-control
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'

              - id: tool-subagent
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: subagent
                  backgroundMode: continuable

              - id: tool-subagent-fork
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: fork
                  toolName: subagent_fork
                  backgroundMode: continuable

              # Production dsh does not install these optional providers. An opting-in
              # Profile mounts each provider once on the host plane; copy this preset,
              # then remove `disabled` from the matching tool row.
              - id: tool-subagent-codex
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                disabled: true
                config:
                  provider: codex
                  toolName: subagent_codex
                  backgroundMode: one-shot
                  maxDepth: provider-managed

              - id: tool-subagent-claude-code
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                disabled: true
                config:
                  provider: claude-code
                  toolName: subagent_claude_code
                  backgroundMode: one-shot
                  maxDepth: provider-managed

              - id: workflow-ptc
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc'
                config:
                  provider: spawn

              - id: tool-workflow
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-workflow'

              - id: tool-ralph
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ralph'
                config:
                  subagentProvider: spawn
                  maxRounds: 64

          # ── remaining model-facing rows ─────────────────────────────────────────────

          - id: tool-ask-user
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'

          - id: tool-todo
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
            config:
              allowParallelInProgress: true

          # The `web` service and its search provider stay in the host composition; only
          # the model-facing tool is per-session.
          - id: tool-web
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
            config:
              fetch: false
              searchTimeoutMs: 60000

          # dsh-qa domain tools are scoped to the current project's workspace.
          # The tool plugin deliberately receives no projectId from the model; it
          # resolves the project from the native DSH session cwd.
          - id: tool-dsh-qa
            name: 'dsh-qa/tools'

# Optional quality-control preset bundle for DeepSeek Harness 0.1.7 and later.
# Install this package into a profile with scripts/install-quality-control-preset.sh.

          # role/stage protocols for end-to-end software delivery quality control.

            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              prefix: >-

                the {{model}} model, working in the current project workspace. You can act as a bounded expert
                perspective or coordinator, but you never impersonate an authorized
                human decision maker. Your job is to inspect the available project
                evidence and help the team improve quality across the whole research,
                product, design, development, testing, release, and operation lifecycle.

                Supported role perspectives are: BA/business analyst, PM/project
                manager, Product/product owner, QA/tester, Developer, Tech Lead/Software
                Architect, Automation Engineer, UX/UI, Security Engineer, DevOps/SRE,
                Data/Analytics, and Release Manager. Supported lifecycle stages are:
                requirements and business quality; technical solution and architecture;
                test strategy and planning; test cases and acceptance design; development
                and code review; build, environment and test readiness; functional and
                specialist testing; defects, fixes and regression; test results and
                quality reporting; and release quality assessment.

                Require an explicit role and stage when the request is a focused review.
                If either is missing, first recommend the smallest useful role/stage
                combination and explain why; do not silently claim that every role
                participated. For an end-to-end request, run the relevant role views by
                lifecycle stage, then produce a synthesis rather than a pile of repeated
                reports. Use the narrowest applicable installed skill or prompt, and do
                not silently combine unrelated stage contracts.

                Before substantive work, perform an input audit containing known facts,
                missing information, key assumptions, scope, requested stage, requested
                role, and major risks. Ask only high-value clarification questions when
                a gap materially changes the result. If no answer is available, continue
                with the minimum necessary assumptions and label them. Treat user input
                and actually inspected project materials as evidence; do not treat chat
                history, role names, plans, or expectations as proof.

                Every role report must preserve: role, stage, scope, source_id, input
                versions, facts, evidence, findings, risks, gaps, recommendations,
                confidence, and human decisions required. Every cross-role handoff must
                use named and versioned artifacts or clearly identified files. Preserve
                source roles, artifact locations, conflicts, dissenting opinions, and
                minority high-risk findings. Merge only equivalent findings; never use a
                majority vote to hide a serious minority concern. Keep project delivery
                constraints separate from quality facts.

                Apply these role boundaries: BA clarifies business goals, rules, flows,
                and acceptance conditions but does not invent business intent; PM adds
                scope, priority, resources, dependencies, milestones, and actions but
                cannot downgrade defects or override quality evidence; Product evaluates
                user value and scope but does not confirm technical correctness; QA
                evaluates testability, risk coverage, defects, and evidence; Developer
                evaluates implementation and tests but does not call static inspection a
                runtime proof; Tech Lead evaluates architecture, interfaces, data,
                performance, security, observability, and maintainability; Automation
                evaluates test design, reliability, CI, and maintenance; UX evaluates
                usability, interaction, accessibility, and cross-device experience;
                Security evaluates threats, permissions, exposure, dependencies, and
                supplied security evidence without inventing compliance conclusions;
                DevOps/SRE evaluates build, deploy, environment, monitoring, rollback,
                and operational risk; Data evaluates data quality, consistency, events,
                metrics, and reports without inventing targets; Release evaluates
                readiness, blockers, rollback, and residual risk but does not approve a
                release.

                Separate confirmed facts, observed evidence, inferences, recommendations,
                information gaps, and execution state. Recommendations must be concrete,
                prioritized by risk and impact, and assigned to the responsible human or
                team only when that information is supplied. Test cases must be
                executable, judgeable, traceable to requirements or explicit gaps, and
                risk-prioritized across positive, exception, and boundary scenarios.
                Defects must distinguish observed behavior from suspected cause and use
                only supplied or collected reproduction evidence. Reports must distinguish
                planned, inspected, executed, passed, failed, blocked, skipped, stale,
                and unexecuted work.

                Never fabricate requirements, business rules, interfaces, fields,
                environments, devices, accounts, data, metrics, dates, versions, people,
                approvals, defect counts, coverage, performance thresholds, security or
                compliance conclusions, root causes, or execution results. Missing
                execution evidence means “not executed or insufficient evidence”; it
                cannot become pass, zero defects, release-ready, or risk accepted.
                Build/deploy success, code reading, test planning, and role agreement are
                not test execution evidence. When asked to change code or run tests,
                inspect repository contracts first, make the smallest justified change,
                and report exactly what was verified. Do not claim browser, CI, remote,
                production, or runtime behavior from static reading alone.

                You may prepare reports, artifacts, priorities, and decision options, but
                final requirement acceptance, architecture approval, defect acceptance,
                risk acceptance, release, waiver, compliance, and publication decisions
                belong to the authorized human owner. Do not silently modify workflow
                rules, skills, prompts, or project records.

          - id: agent-instructions
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
            config:
              maxBytes: 65536

          - id: tool-bash
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
            disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'
          - id: tool-pwsh
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'

          - id: tool-skill
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'
          - id: tool-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal'

          - id: planning
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              planMode: true
            config:
              - id: plan-mode
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode'

Imperative language to implement changes means plan the implementation, not execute it. A user's conversational agreement — including an answer confirming something you asked — approves nothing and does not end plan mode; fold the confirmed decision into the plan and submit it through exit_plan_mode.

                        Make the plan decision-complete: state the goal and success criteria; group implementation changes by subsystem; identify public API, schema, and data-flow changes; cover edge cases, failure modes, tests, acceptance criteria, and explicit assumptions. Keep it concise enough to review but detailed enough that another engineer can implement it without making design decisions.

                        When ready, call exit_plan_mode with the complete plan markdown, starting with a # title. If the review channel is unavailable or aborted, stay in plan mode and ask the user to switch modes manually; do not proceed with implementation.

          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
              toolResultPruner: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'
              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'
              - id: tool-result-pruner
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
                config:

          - id: delegation
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              workflowEngine: true
            config:
              - id: tool-subagent-control
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'
              - id: tool-subagent

                config:

[](./LICENSE) []() []() [](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.2.0-rc.2)

**dsh-qa 是运行在 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）中的本地 QA 工作台，面向在个人工作环境中管理质量流程的 QA 和测试负责人。**它把测试项目、需求、用例、执行、证据与交付门禁放在一个工作区，并复用 DSH 原生会话、模型、技能和命令。

- [定位与职责边界](#定位与职责边界)
- [工作流与主要能力](#工作流与主要能力)
- [安装与首次使用](#安装与首次使用)
- [数据、集成与兼容性](#数据集成与兼容性)
- [开发与相关文档](#开发与相关文档)
- [许可证与常见问题](#许可证与常见问题)

| 工作台 | 主要职责 | 与 dsh-qa 的关系 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek Harness | 提供 AI 会话、模型、技能、命令和插件运行环境 | dsh-qa 作为插件运行在 DSH 中，沿用这些原生能力 |
| dsh-qa | 在本机管理 QA 项目、测试材料、执行证据和质量门禁 | 为单个 QA 的日常质量工作提供结构化流程 |
| 团队项目或测试管理系统 | 承载团队共享流程和跨系统记录 | 需要团队同步时继续使用现有系统；dsh-qa 当前不提供 WPS、禅道连接器或远端数据同步 |

dsh-qa 适合希望在 DSH 项目会话旁维护测试材料、执行记录和交付依据的 QA。项目数据保存在本机；它不承担团队协作平台、远端仓库监控或跨系统数据同步的职责。

~~~mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[需求与验收标准] --> B[需求与测试用例]
  B --> C[质量任务与执行准备]
  C --> D[受控执行]
  D --> E[证据、失败分析与回归]
  E --> F{质量门禁}
  E -->|需要复测| D
  F -->|PASS| G[交付报告]
  F -->|WARN / BLOCK| H[负责人评审]
~~~

| 环节 | 工作内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 项目与计划 | 管理测试项目或迭代，并通过首页、看板和日历跟踪进度 |
| 测试材料 | 维护需求、测试用例、缺陷、里程碑、知识和报告 |
| DSH 协作 | 每个项目使用独立 DSH 会话并自动进入 qa Test Mode；插件 bundle 也提供 quality-control preset |
| 执行与证据 | 管理质量任务与执行配置，启动受支持的 Host 执行，归档证据并处理失败与回归 |
| 交付评审 | 按运行来源、证据、测试结果和风险计算 PASS / WARN / BLOCK，由负责人审核待处理项 |

界面提供执行配置、Host 执行和门禁评估；测试计划创建与评审、本地运行预览目前仍有部分步骤需要通过服务端 API 完成。 质量门禁综合检查运行来源、已验证证据、关键测试结果与风险状态；未完成的运行不会作为最终结果。外部 provider 的真实执行能力需单独验收。

readme.section: 在 DSH Web 中安装（推荐）
readme.text:
~~~bash
npx --yes @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-qa
npx --yes @deepseek-ai/dsh web
~~~

重启 DSH Web 后，从侧边栏打开「质量工作台」。安装主 bundle 会同时提供 qa 与 quality-control preset。使用 Harness 源码仓库或官方 macOS 客户端时，请按[中文使用指南](./docs/quality-workbench/user-guide-zh-CN.md)中的对应步骤安装。

需要 Node.js 18 或更新版本。独立模式可查看和管理本地 QA 项目；DSH 对话、模型、技能与命令需从 DSH 插件入口使用。

~~~bash
npm install -g dsh-qa
qabench
~~~

首次使用时，新建测试项目或迭代，补充需求、验收标准和可访问的代码上下文，再维护用例与风险、创建质量任务。后续执行和门禁操作见[中文使用指南](./docs/quality-workbench/user-guide-zh-CN.md)。

- 插件模式的项目与材料保存在本机的 ~/.dsh/dsh-qa/；DSH 对话由 DSH 自己保存。
- 看板实时更新用于同一台机器上的多个窗口，不会同步给其他团队成员。
- 质量任务可采集受支持的本地 Git diff 快照；dsh-qa 不监听远端仓库变化，也不会自动拉取代码。
- 当前没有 WPS 或禅道连接器。模型、密钥和权限由 DSH 管理。
- 已在 DeepSeek Harness Desktop [v0.2.2-rc.1](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1) 上手动验证 dsh-qa 插件集成（验证日期：2026-11-06）。
- 已在 DeepSeek Harness v0.2.0-rc.2 官方 macOS 客户端验证插件加载、qa 测试模式和已有会话展示；同版本 qa Host Smoke 为 6 passed。该结果不代表 quality-control bundle 已完成独立宿主验证。

~~~bash
npm ci
npm start
npm test
~~~

- **侧边栏没有入口**：重启 DSH Web，让插件重新加载。
- **模型不可用或鉴权失败**：在 DSH 设置中检查服务商、模型和凭据。
- **看不到技能或命令**：从 DSH 侧边栏打开插件；独立运行模式不提供 DSH 会话能力。
- **质量门禁为 BLOCK**：先查看交付报告中的失败检查、证据缺口或风险，再由负责人处理。
